summary: Backend-only auth regression suite for P0 multi-device session persistence passed on public preview URL, including requested Phase41 and Iter34 tests plus an added suspended-user check.
action_items: No backend auth blocking defects found in requested scope.
Run separate frontend test pass for P1 login password visibility toggle (not executed in this backend-only cycle).
Optional maintenance: migrate FastAPI deprecated on_event handlers to lifespan handlers.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.refresh now preserves token_version and sid from refresh token payload; this prevents unintended cross-device logout and keeps same-device session continuity.
auth + auth_utils correctly enforce token_version checks for both access and refresh paths, enabling global revocation behavior.
FastAPI startup/shutdown uses deprecated on_event API (warning observed during tests); migrate to lifespan to avoid future framework breakage.
seed_data_creation: Temporary auth users were created in tests (phase41 + iter37) and cleaned up in finally blocks; test_seed_admin_updates_existing_admin_when_password_changes restores original hash in cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Executed requested backend scope only. Phase41 multi-device behavior, tv revocation, disabled and suspended status handling, secure HttpOnly cookie issuance, bearer fallback, brute-force lockout, bcrypt seed hash format, and seed-admin password repair are green on preview endpoint.
rca of the issue: Previously reproduced issue was refresh issuing tv=0, causing device A invalidation after refresh when user token_version>0. Current behavior validates payload tv against user token_version and reissues access/refresh with current token_version + preserved sid; regression no longer reproduces. No API flow is MOCKED.
